text:
Maya S.: fyi forwarding an escalated ticket from Acme — their mobile clients frequently drop mid-stream and when they reconnect they only get the last partial event; sometimes there are duplicate partial chunks. customer pasted logs + curl repro.

Devon K.: thanks — can you paste the original client repro? is this SSE or chunked HTTP?

Maya S.: SSE. customer says it happens when users switch from cell -> wifi or when the phone screen locks. they see a streak of partial tokens then the connection closes. they use our hosted API endpoint `https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream` with an auth token. excerpt from customer: 

> "on android, I switch from 5g to home wifi, stream stops at ~30 tokens, reconnect sends Last-Event-ID but server returns full new response from start, and sometimes the UI shows a garbled partial line then a new stream — they patch client to dedupe but it's messy."

Liam P.: do we have any 499/connection aborted spikes in the edge logs for that org at the reported times? what client IPs/regions?

SSE Bot: automated-log-scan: found 12 requests with 499 (client closed) and 200/stream aborted entries for org_id=acme-corp between 2024-11-02T15:40:02Z and 2024-11-02T16:04:21Z. Average RTT 180ms, median tokens before abort 28. Samples: `req_id=rr_8f2a, remote_ip=34.82.190.12, reason=TCP_RST`

Anna R.: that matches mobile handoff pattern. two hypotheses: 1) client aborts TCP (mobile stacks often send RST on active handoff) so server receives a connection close and can't flush full SSE events; 2) client reconnect attempts but doesn't set `Last-Event-ID` correctly or server's stream event `id:` value isn't stable, so resume logic fails.

Devon K.: do we set `id:` on every SSE event? i think our runtime only sets `id:` every N tokens (to avoid overhead). if Last-Event-ID is older than last committed id we might replay from earlier boundary which looks like duplicate/partial.

Liam P.: that's important — customer says they send `Last-Event-ID: 1623` and get overlapping content. we should check if our SSE encoder includes a final `id:` before connection close. if not, client can't resume precisely.

Maya S.: customer provided curl repro. posting as-is: 

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rw-instruct" \
  --no-buffer
```

Customer then simulates network drop by toggling interface; on reconnect they do: 

```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Last-Event-ID: 1623" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=rw-instruct&resume=true"
```
They say sometimes server returns a new stream from 0, sometimes resumes but with a partial last event.

Devon K.: steps I'm going to take: 1) check runtime SSE encoder config for `event id` frequency; 2) inspect edge proxy (nginx/envoy) config for streaming timeouts / keepalive / `proxy_buffering` and if we translate Last-Event-ID correctly to backend; 3) search logs for `resume=true` handling and failures.

Anna R.: also capture the client-side symptom: partial event means we wrote an `data:` block that got truncated mid-chunk — SSE semantics say an event is delimited by a blank line; if TCP closed mid-event, client receives partial and there's no delimiter. When they reconnect with Last-Event-ID pointing to the previous event id, server may re-emit the full event; client-level dedupe is necessary. but good server behavior: emit `id:` more frequently (per event) and on connection close try to flush a final event boundary if possible.

Liam P.: dev note: mobile handoffs often cause immediate TCP RST so server may not be able to flush. two mitigations: 1) the client should implement idempotent event handling and de-dup on `id`; 2) server can emit smaller, more frequent events (e.g., commit every 8-16 tokens with `id:`) to reduce amount of re-streamed content and avoid large partials.

Devon K.: found config: runtime has `sse_commit_interval=64_tokens` default. that explains why partials are large. lowering to 16 reduces worst-case re-stream by ~4x. but need perf test. also edge proxy has `proxy_read_timeout 60s` and `send_timeout 60s` — those are fine; more relevant is `proxy_buffering off` is set, good. I also saw a few entries where our load balancer closed idle connections after 30s — that's relevant if clients pause during handoff.

SSE Bot: repro-scan: generated a test using headless android emulator and toggled mobile->wifi — reproduced 2/5 times with current config (64 tokens commit). Fail mode: client got partial `data:` (no trailing blank line), then client reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` resumed from the last committed id and caused duplicate prefix.

Anna R.: recommended immediate support response to customer: explain cause and short-term mitigations client-side + server-side. propose these action items: 
- set `sse_commit_interval` to 16 for affected tenant (can be an org-specific override) as a short-term config change (low risk).
- advise client to implement id-based dedupe and exponential backoff on reconnects; show exact SSE handling snippet.
- long-term: make runtime flush an extra final event boundary on accepted signal of socket close if kernel sends FIN (best-effort).

Maya S.: drafting reply. wanna include a simple client snippet for dedupe. Anna, can you paste the snippet?

Anna R.: sure — example JS worker logic: 

```
// client SSE reconnection dedupe
const seen = new Set();
const es = new EventSource(url);
es.onmessage = (ev) => {
  if (seen.has(ev.lastEventId)) return; // dedupe
  seen.add(ev.lastEventId);
  // handle ev.data
};
// on reconnect, send Last-Event-ID header (polyfill for EventSource)
```

Devon K.: I'll open a small internal change to set `sse_commit_interval=16` for org_id=acme-corp as a test for 24h and monitor token replays and latency. also will add a short-term dashboard showing resume/failure rate.

Liam P.: I'll add an entry to the runtime backlog to evaluate emitting more frequent `id:` and to try best-effort flush on FIN. also add tests to our streaming e2e for mobile handoffs.

Maya S.: customer reply drafted: explains we see mobile handoff RSTs, propose config tweak + client dedupe snippet + offer 24h trial of org override. will send and wait for repro confirmation. adding ticket link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-3321

Devon K.: notes for follow-up: monitor for duplicates after change, check token costs (more frequent ids slightly increase bandwidth), and confirm no regressions in high-throughput dedicated customers.

Anna R.: final: include suggestion for client to use exponential backoff + jitter for reconnect and to wait 200-500ms before resuming after interface change — avoids thundering reconnections to edge. :thumbsup:

Maya S.: thanks team — I sent the message to Acme with proposed steps. will update thread with their response. :white_check_mark:
